title: Zeros or X-Intercepts
text: The radicand $$\frac{7}{x-5}$$ can never equal $$0$$ because its numerator is $$7$$, so the function has no zero.

title: Domain
text: For a real square root, require $$\frac{7}{x-5}>0$$. Since the numerator is positive, this gives $$x>5$$.

title: Range
text: The output is always positive. It grows without bound near $$x=5$$ and approaches $$0$$ without reaching it as $$x$$ increases.
